title: Terms of Account: Stop Payment Orders on Personal Checking Paper Checks
content:
A stop payment order on a Personal Checking account covers one paper check, identified by the check serial number and the exact amount the customer states; the payee is recorded as the customer states it.

**Conditions.**

1. Stop payment orders are available only on a tier on which paper checks can be written.
2. A stop payment can be placed only on a check that has not already been paid. A check counts as paid when a paid-check debit bearing the same serial number stands on the account.
3. A second order on a check that already has an unexpired order is not placed; the existing order is renewed instead.

**Duration and renewal.** An order lapses at the end of 6 calendar months after the date it was placed: its lapse date is the order date plus 6 calendar months, falling back to the last day of the month where that day does not exist. An unexpired order may be renewed on or before its lapse date. Count calendar months from the order date of the order being renewed; renewal is allowed while the frozen date is on or before that order's lapse date. A renewal is recorded against the order being renewed, and its own lapse date is the renewal date plus 6 calendar months. A lapsed order cannot be renewed; a fresh order is placed instead if the check is still unpaid.

**Stops outside this basis.** Stops on direct debits and on official checks are outside this basis.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical).** An order placed on the 31st of a month lapses on the 30th of the month 6 months later, that month having no 31st. A renewal asked for on the lapse day itself is allowed, because the comparison is not-later-than and the boundary day satisfies it; a renewal asked for the day after is not, and the check, if still unpaid, takes a fresh order instead.
